quick.summary: How to prevent stakeholders from derailing your presentation with predictable objections.
quick.takeaway: Say the biggest downside out loud before your audience can complain about it.

beats.line: They debated the new layout forever. How do I stop the arguing?
Think of a tour guide warning you about a steep hill.
You know it is coming, so you just walk.
Right. Do this for controversial design choices too.
In debate, this is called a preemptive rebuttal.
Can I just say name the worry? Refutation sounds so aggressive.
Name the worry works perfectly here.
Say the downside out loud before they can complain.
So I admit the image gets pushed down, right away.
Yes. Then you explain why it is the right choice.
This drops the image, but it converts much better.
And the steep hill is cleared.

quiz.question: What is the primary benefit of naming a downside before your audience brings it up?
options: It stops them from asking questions entirely.
It hides the issue in the middle of your presentation.
It frames you as honest and defuses their biggest worry.
It makes the meeting end much faster.
quiz.explanation: When you name the worry first, you show you have already thought about their concerns, which builds trust.

quiz.question: Pointing out a flaw in your own design during a pitch makes you look unprepared.
quiz.explanation: It actually makes you look highly prepared. You control the narrative instead of getting defensive later.
